notes:
Passed the fake backend only; evidence is contract_checked, never an MHS-Device level and never a hardware run. The package binds the camera resource of the upstream repository: the reads and scalar writes of robocam.camera:Camera, the native Camera.stop() as the e-stop, and the capture-counter reset as an x-cap action. The repository's three-axis motion system and laser output are separate upstream classes and are not part of this device manifest. NOT COVERED: the image and raw image arrays from Camera.get_frame() and Camera.get_raw_frame() (the standard's image form is an artifact reference and this package has no artifact store), and the application's motion and laser controls. Limits: usb_bandwidth_percent is bounded to 35 to 100 percent by robocam/camera.py:387 (setter clamp at line 399); no text states a bound for exposure_us, gain, offset or sensor_mode_index, so each is Limit.operator_required and every write is refused MHS.SAFETY.LIMITS_UNSET until site-limits.json supplies it. site-limits.example.json fills those four paths with placeholder example values only; it is not a measurement or a statement about any installed camera. DEVIATION FROM THE CARD: mock_strategy.preferred is upstream-sim, but the task forbids importing or running the clone, so fake.py is a package in-memory fake over the same method names; its starting values are test data marked placeholder, not facts. The package is model-authored and unreviewed (driver.lock.json reviewed_by is null), so it makes no claim of human review or testing.
